text:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: SEV1 alert — customer 'Silverline' p99 latency spike in eu-west dedicated pool (pool-id: dp-eu-west-11). Alert rule: dedicated_pool_latency_p99 > 2000ms for 5m. Links: https://metrics.redwood/s/alerts/3201234567, runbook: https://confluence.redwood/incident-playbooks/dedicated-latency

Ryan: oncall here. Acknowledging. Pulling graphs now.

Maya: looking at tail latency — p50 ~120ms, p95 ~350ms, p99 ~2.3s. GPU util for pool dp-eu-west-11 at 96%, but NVLINK queues also show stalls. Top offending tenant appears to be silverline-tenant-42 (traffic burst + long contexts).

Julien: can you paste the slow-op sample from the runtime logs? suspect KV cache churn + kernel fallback causing logits stalls.

Maya: pasting tail logs: ```
2026-03-15T03:12:07Z [dp-eu-west-11] tenant=silverline-tenant-42 req_id=tx-9f2a slow_op=kernel_fallback seq_len=4096 tokens=1024 gpu_util=98% kv_miss=0.73
2026-03-15T03:12:09Z [dp-eu-west-11] tenant=silverline-tenant-42 req_id=tx-9f2b slow_op=attention_matmul latency_ms=1320
```

Ash: cc @Leo — customer CS/PS on call? Silverline on live promo so high impact. Leo: please advise if we should auto-open a support bridge.

Leo: Silverline escalation team is on the bridge. They're seeing timeouts in their app and have degraded UX. They've asked for mitigation asap and want comms to customers within 30m.

Ryan: immediate mitigations I'm trying now: 1) throttle tenant (soft) to reduce concurrency; 2) enable tenant isolation routing to move silverline-tenant-42 to isolated nodes; 3) spin up warm spare in eu-west-2 and cut a percentage of traffic.

Maya: runbook steps executed: ```
# throttle to 30rps per-tenant
redwoodctl rate-limit set --pool dp-eu-west-11 --tenant silverline-tenant-42 --rps 30

# mark tenant for isolation (evict to dedicated isolation set)
redwoodctl tenant isolate --tenant silverline-tenant-42 --pool dp-eu-west-11
```

inc-bot: Action taken: rate-limit applied and tenant isolation flag set. Pager remains open.

Julien: while isolation starts, prepare model fallback: recommend moving Silverline to quantized-compat-1 (smaller memory footprint) for short term — cuts token latency ~45% in lab. Can we do a fast switch?

Maya: isolation completed — silverline-tenant-42 now on isolation nodes (node-set: iso-eu-west-11a). Observed immediate drop in cross-tenant interference. p99 down to ~1.4s but still above SLO. GPU util on iso nodes ~92%.

Ryan: spinning a warm pool in eu-west-2 and starting traffic siphon. Command: ```
redwoodctl pool clone --source dp-eu-west-11 --target dp-eu-west-2-warm --size 4gpus --profile low-latency
redwoodctl routing set --tenant silverline-tenant-42 --percent 20 --target dp-eu-west-2-warm
```

Ash: Can we apply automatic KV cache warm-up for the tenant to avoid cold-cache penalties when moving nodes? That's been the main cause of sequence stall historically.

Julien: yes — enabling prefix cache warmup for the tenant now. Also lowering max_seq_length to 2048 for active traffic to reduce memory pressure. ```
redwoodctl cache warmup --tenant silverline-tenant-42 --samples 500
redwoodctl model config set --tenant silverline-tenant-42 --max_seq_length 2048
```

Maya: warmup in progress; metrics show request latency on the warm pool is healthy ~200ms p95. Redirected 35% now. p99 global for silverline traffic ~850ms and trending down.

Leo: notifying customer (short comms): "We're seeing elevated latencies affecting a subset of requests. We've isolated the workload, rerouting to a warm spare region, and expect progressive improvement. Will update in 20m."

Sam: I'm taking the handoff in 40 minutes. Will watch for regression and ensure rollback plan is ready.

Ryan: plan B if p99 doesn't drop below 500ms in 15m: 1) force full cutover to hosted fallback model variant (hosted-fallback-small) for degraded but reliable service; 2) schedule eviction of any other noisy tenants on iso nodes.

Maya: quick note — I see intermittent kernel fallback on iso nodes at ~2% of requests; likely due to rare ops in Silverline prompt. Julien, can runtime patch disable that kernel path temporarily?

Julien: yes, pushing a conservative kernel config to prefer quantized matmul kernels. Rolling to iso-eu-west-11a now (1/3 canary): ```
redwoodctl runtime config set --name prefer_quant_kernels=true --nodes iso-eu-west-11a --canary 33
```

inc-bot: update: canary applied (33%). Monitoring.

Maya: after canary, kernel fallback events drop to 0.3% and p99 for silverline traffic steady ~520ms. We're close.

Leo: Silverline wants ETA for full recovery. I'm going to propose a 30 min window given current trajectory.

Ryan: agree. Continue traffic siphon to warm pool to 80% in 10m if metrics remain stable. Keep hosted fallback as last resort.

Ash: internal note for postmortem: customer had a sudden increase in very long context requests (~10% of their traffic spiked to >8k tokens). This is outside their normal profile and should be flagged for PS.

Maya: metrics checkpoint at 03:20Z: p50=110ms p95=240ms p99=480ms for silverline across pools. GPU util down to 68% overall.

Sam: taking handoff early. Confirmed runbook actions, warm pool stable, customer comms sent. I'll stay until metrics stable for 2 consecutive 5m buckets.

Ryan: thanks. Leaving notes: root cause next steps: 1) get customer's request profile & prompt set; 2) verify tenant rate limits & autoscale config; 3) recommend per-tenant model profiling & sequence-length caps; 4) add an alert for sudden long-context spike.

inc-bot: SEV1 acknowledged -> transitioned to monitoring. Incident will remain open until Sam confirms stable baseline.

Julien: logging action items to the incident tracker: https://incidents.redwood/3201234567. I'll prepare a small runtime patch to avoid kernel fallback in short term and coordinate a safer kernel switch in the morning if needed.

Leo: customer requested a follow-up doc and timeline for permanent mitigation. I'll coordinate PS engagement.

Sam: closing note (03:28Z): metrics stable; p99 < 500ms for past 3 mins; keeping monitoring window 60m. If no regression, we'll transition to postmortem phase and produce customer-friendly timeline. :thumbsup:
